title: Failure Mode Analysis: Where Do Safety Scores Break Down Under Adversarial User Personas?
original_idea: Test 150 harmful prompts each under three persona conditions: no persona, benign professional persona, and expert persona plausibly requiring the information. Measure refusal rates across conditions for three models.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Persona-based manipulation is a real-world attack vector. Demonstrating that benchmarks underestimate failure rates by ignoring personas is practically significant.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prepend persona text to prompts, run through models, measure refusal rates. Straightforward prompt manipulation and API usage. Accessible for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 150 prompts x 3 conditions x 3 models is well-defined. Clear experimental structure. Feasible in 30 hours with medium compute.

novelty.reasoning: Persona-based jailbreak attacks are extensively studied. 'Enhancing Jailbreak Attacks on LLMs via Persona Prompts' (arXiv:2507.22171, 2025) demonstrates that evolved persona prompts reduce refusal rates by 50-70% across multiple LLMs. TeleAI-Safety (arXiv:2512.05485, 2025) integrates 19 attack methods including persona-based approaches. JailbreakBench provides standardized evaluation. The MLCommons Jailbreak Benchmark v0.5 (Dec 2025) measures system adversarial resilience. The proposed experiment — testing harmful prompts under no-persona, benign-professional, and expert personas — is a simpler version of what has been comprehensively studied with genetic algorithm-optimized persona prompts and systematic attack taxonomies.
